es.summary: Los medicamentos genéricos deben demostrar bioequivalencia y eficacia comparable al producto de referencia para ser aprobados. Su uso brinda ahorro sin comprometer la efectividad clínica.
key_points: Los genéricos deben probar bioequivalencia (±20% del AUC y Cmax del original).
La FDA exige evidencia de eficacia y seguridad antes de la aprobación.
Los ensayos de eficacia se realizan en el fármaco de referencia; los genéricos replican la formulación.
La percepción del paciente puede influir en la adherencia al genérico.
Los genéricos pueden presentar variaciones inactivas, pero no alteran la respuesta terapéutica.
Los profesionales deben educar sobre la equivalencia terapéutica.

nursing_care: Verificar que el genérico tenga la misma DCI y forma farmacéutica que el original.
Revisar la etiqueta para confirmar la concentración y vía de administración.
Monitorear la respuesta clínica del paciente al iniciar el genérico.
Reportar cualquier reacción adversa inesperada al farmacovigilancia.
patient_teaching: Explicar que la eficacia del genérico es equivalente al del medicamento de referencia.
Asegurar que el paciente comprenda que el costo menor no implica menor calidad.
Instruir sobre la importancia de no interrumpir el tratamiento por dudas de efectividad.

outcomes: Conocimiento del paciente: demostrar comprensión de la equivalencia terapéutica del genérico en 2 semanas.
Adherencia al tratamiento: mantener >90% de dosis tomadas según prescripción en 1 mes.

interventions.action: Proveer información escrita y verbal sobre la bioequivalencia del genérico
interventions.rationale: Facilita la comprensión y reduce dudas.

interventions.action: Comparar etiquetas del genérico y del de referencia con el paciente
Responder preguntas y corregir mitos sobre la eficacia
interventions.rationale: Previene la desinformación que afecta la adherencia.

interventions.action: Evaluar comprensión mediante preguntas de retorno
interventions.rationale: Confirma que el paciente haya internalizado la información.

en.summary: Generic drugs must demonstrate bioequivalence and comparable efficacy to the reference product to be approved. Their use provides savings without compromising clinical effectiveness.
key_points: Generics must prove bioequivalence (±20% of the original's AUC and Cmax).
The FDA requires evidence of efficacy and safety before approval.
Efficacy trials are conducted on the reference drug; generics replicate the formulation.
Patient perception can influence adherence to the generic.
Generics may have inactive variations, but they do not alter therapeutic response.
Professionals must educate about therapeutic equivalence.

nursing_care: Verify that the generic has the same active ingredient and dosage form as the original.
Check the label to confirm concentration and route of administration.
Monitor the patient's clinical response when starting the generic.
Report any unexpected adverse reactions to pharmacovigilance.
patient_teaching: Explain that the generic's efficacy is equivalent to the reference medication.
Ensure the patient understands that lower cost does not imply lower quality.
Instruct on the importance of not discontinuing treatment due to doubts about effectiveness.

outcomes: Patient knowledge: demonstrate understanding of therapeutic equivalence of the generic within 2 weeks.
Treatment adherence: maintain >90% of prescribed doses taken within 1 month.

interventions.action: Provide written and verbal information about the generic's bioequivalence
Compare the generic and reference labels with the patient
Answer questions and correct myths about efficacy

interventions.rationale: Confirms that the patient has internalized the information.

summary.0.quote: A company manufacturing a generic drug has to demonstrate that the drug is bioequivalent to the brand-name drug, whereas a company developing and producing a biosimilar drug must demonstrate that it is similar to the biologic it is patterned after (called the reference drug).

summary.1.quote: Companies that manufacture generic drugs must test to ensure equivalency, but they do not have to redo the efficacy trials.

key_points.1.quote: Once a chemical that may have therapeutic effects is isolated, it will undergo scientific tests and clinical trials to prove its efficacy and safety.

key_points.2.quote: Companies that manufacture generic drugs must test to ensure equivalency, but they do not have to redo the efficacy trials.

sections.nursing_care.0.quote: According to the FDA (2021a), a generic drug is manufactured with the intent that it is identical in the active chemical ingredients, safety, strength, quality, dosage form, and intended use as its brand name counterpart.
